title: kith-events: in-process state change channel
description:
What: Define StateChange type in kith-core, create broadcast channel infrastructure in kith-events, add events_tx field to Store and AppState.

Algorithm:
1. crates/kith-core/src/lib.rs (or new mod events): pub struct StateChange { pub type_name: String, pub new_state: String } with #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]; re-export from kith_core root
2. crates/kith-events/src/lib.rs: pub use kith_core::StateChange; pub use tokio::sync::broadcast::{Sender as EventSender, Receiver as EventReceiver}; pub fn make_channel(capacity: usize) -> (EventSender<StateChange>, EventReceiver<StateChange>) wrapping tokio::sync::broadcast::channel(capacity)
3. crates/kith-store/src/lib.rs - Store struct: add field pub events_tx: Option<tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<kith_core::StateChange>> defaulting to None; add pub fn set_events_tx(&mut self, tx: tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<kith_core::StateChange>)
4. crates/kithd/src/extractors.rs - AppState<W>: add field pub events_tx: tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<kith_events::StateChange> (Sender is already Arc-backed; no additional Arc needed)
5. cargo check -p kith-core -p kith-events -p kith-store -p kithd

Defensive rules:
- StateChange must derive Clone (broadcast requires T: Clone)
- Recommended channel capacity: 64 (use in tests and kithd startup)
- kith-core must NOT depend on tokio; StateChange is a plain data struct
- AppState holds Sender (not Receiver); each SSE client calls subscribe() for its own Receiver
- No key material or PII in StateChange fields
